summary: Re-ran every gate the software-engineer claimed (app lint/typecheck/test/build, orchestrator typecheck/test, pack hygiene) from a clean invocation, independent of their claims, and all reproduced exactly as reported EXCEPT app-test, which now fails because of 2 new tests I added that reproduce real production bugs (not test bugs). Added 6 new test files (39 new test cases) covering all 5 verificationTargets: parseDuelInvite (18 cases), formatElapsed (7 cases), computeWeekDays (6 cases), a DuelHome smoke render (3 cases, signed-out/signed-in/anonymous), a ClimbBoard smoke render (3 cases, populated/unavailable/empty), and a ClimbBoard viewer-panel fetch-fallback test (2 cases, non-200 vs rejected fetch, asserting the standings <ol> markup is byte-identical between the two failure modes). Proved the parseDuelInvite negative-fixture gate is not tautological: temporarily loosened src/lib/duelInvite.ts's regexes/protocol-check (diff captured, then reverted via cp from a pre-edit backup — `git diff` on the file is now empty, confirming an exact revert) and confirmed 13 of my 18 assertions correctly flipped red, including the javascript:, protocol-relative, data:, too-short, too-long and disallowed-character fixtures. Found two real gaps while doing this: (1) parseDuelInvite does NOT reject cross-origin absolute URLs whose path matches /duel/<id> (AC-10 explicitly requires rejecting 'cross-origin URLs'; https://evil.dev/duel/<validId> currently returns the id, not null) — low security impact since the caller only ever uses the returned ID to build a same-origin route, never the input URL or its host, but it is a real, reproducible AC-10 non-conformance; (2) formatElapsed(NaN) returns the string 'NaN:NaN' instead of clamping to '0:00' as explicitly specified in the software-engineer's own verificationTargets entry (`Math.max(0, Math.floor(NaN))` is NaN, not 0, so the clamp silently no-ops on non-finite input). Both are genuine defects in current production code, not test artifacts — full detail and repro below.

findings.issue: AC-10 (loop/spec-doomstack-layout.md) explicitly requires parseDuelInvite to return null for cross-origin URLs. extractPath only validates the URL's scheme (http/https) and takes url.pathname — it never compares the URL's origin/host against the app's own origin. Repro: parseDuelInvite('https://evil.dev/duel/abcdef123456') returns 'abcdef123456' instead of null (see app/tests/lib/duelInvite.test.ts, 'cross-origin URL with an otherwise-valid /duel/<id> path', which fails against current production code — this is a real gap, not a test bug; I proved the gate itself is meaningful by deliberately loosening the parser and watching 13 of 18 assertions correctly flip red first).
findings.fix: Either (a) add an origin check in extractPath — e.g. thread window.location.origin (or an injected expectedOrigin param, to keep the function pure/testable) and reject when url.origin differs — or (b) if the product decision is that origin doesn't matter because only the parsed id is ever used to build the same-origin route (the module's own docstring already argues this), amend AC-10's wording in loop/spec-doomstack-layout.md to drop the cross-origin-URL requirement so the spec matches the intended design. Security impact is low either way: the caller (DuelHome.tsx:298) always does router.push('/duel/' + duelId) from the PARSED id, never the raw input or its host, so no open redirect or cross-origin navigation is reachable today — but the written AC and the shipped behavior disagree, and a future caller could reasonably assume parseDuelInvite enforces same-origin because the AC says it does.

findings.issue: The software-engineer's own verificationTargets entry states 'negative/NaN clamps to 0:00', but Math.max(0, Math.floor(NaN)) evaluates to NaN (Math.max propagates NaN regardless of the other argument), so formatElapsed(NaN) returns the string 'NaN:NaN', not '0:00'. Repro in app/tests/components/duelHomeFormatElapsed.test.ts ('NaN input clamps to 0:00'), which fails against current production code.
findings.fix: Guard with Number.isFinite before the clamp, e.g. `const safe = Number.isFinite(totalSeconds) ? Math.max(0, Math.floor(totalSeconds)) : 0;`. No production caller currently feeds NaN (useElapsedSeconds always produces a non-negative integer counter), so this has zero live-bug impact today, but the function is exported and the stated contract should hold for any future caller.

verificationNotes: Confirmed the handoff's SSR-bailout note is accurate and accounted for it: app/app/duel/page.tsx wraps DuelHome in <Suspense> and DuelHome calls useSearchParams directly, so a curl/fetch of the /duel route is not evidence of anything — my DuelHome smoke test renders the DuelHome REACT COMPONENT directly (next/navigation and AuthContext mocked) via renderToStaticMarkup instead of hitting the route, which is the approach the handoff asked me to confirm.

vitest.config.ts runs environment: node by default (renderToStaticMarkup only — no effects execute). ClimbBoard's viewer-panel fetch only runs inside a useEffect, so AC-17 coverage required a real mount: used the existing tests/hooks/useMatchmakingQueue.test.ts pattern (react-dom/client createRoot + act, `@vitest-environment happy-dom` file-level pragma) rather than introducing a new testing-library dependency (none is installed in app/).

First attempt at the ClimbBoard viewer-panel test hung a vitest worker at 100%+ CPU indefinitely: my AuthContext mock returned a NEW object literal on every call, so ClimbBoard's `useEffect([user, token, authLoading])` saw a new `user` reference every render and looped (setState -> rerender -> new mock object -> effect refires -> setState -> ...). Fixed by hoisting the mock auth state to a stable module-level object. Flagging for reviewer/qa-acceptance: any future test that mocks a hook consumed inside a useEffect dependency array must return a referentially-stable value, or it can hang the whole test run rather than fail fast.
Confirmed via `git status --short app/api` and `git diff --stat HEAD -- app/api` that no API route files changed in this pass, consistent with the 'no new endpoints' claim.

Environment note (not a finding, for the record): partway through this session app/tests/lib/duelInvite.test.ts, app/tests/lib/dailyWeek.test.ts, app/tests/components/duelHomeFormatElapsed.test.ts, and app/tests/components/duelHomeSmoke.test.tsx appeared already committed under the software-engineer's existing commit (b63dd6a) without me running `git commit` — some snapshot/auto-commit mechanism in this sandbox folded them in. I did not commit or push anything myself. app/tests/components/climbBoardSmoke.test.tsx and app/tests/components/climbBoardViewerPanel.test.tsx (written later in the session) remain uncommitted/untracked in the working tree, along with unrelated Next.js build artifacts (app/next-env.d.ts, app/AGENTS.md, app/CLAUDE.md) that next dev/build regenerates and are not my changes.

learnings.insight: parseDuelInvite(NaN-adjacent bug class): Math.max(0, Math.floor(NaN)) is NaN, not 0 — Math.max/Math.min propagate NaN through any argument position. A 'clamp to 0' guard needs an explicit Number.isFinite check, not just Math.max(0, ...).
learnings.action: Grep this codebase for other `Math.max(0, Math.floor(<external input>))` clamps that claim to handle NaN/negative and verify each one actually does.

learnings.insight: parseDuelInvite's own module docstring claims 'no open redirect is reachable' because the caller only uses the parsed id — that claim is true and I verified the only call site (DuelHome.tsx:298) does build the route from the parsed id, never the raw string. But the written spec (AC-10) additionally promises cross-origin URLs are rejected outright, and the code does not do that (it accepts https://any-host/duel/<id> and returns the id). The security claim in the code comment holds; the acceptance-criteria claim in the spec does not. These are two different bars and only the weaker one (no open redirect) is actually met.
learnings.action: When a module's docstring asserts a security property, verify that claim specifically — it is not automatically equivalent to whatever the acceptance criteria describe with similar-sounding language ('cross-origin URLs ... rejected').

learnings.insight: Post-verification baseline: app/ now has 85 test files / 777 tests (775 pass, 2 documented production-bug failures — see findings). lint/typecheck/hygiene/orchestrator all clean. next build succeeds with unchanged route rendering modes (/ ISR 1m, /climb dynamic, /daily static, /duel static).
learnings.action: Treat any test-count drop below 775-passing, or any rendering-mode flip, as a regression introduced after this handoff.

learnings.insight: Mocking a hook (e.g. useAuth) that is consumed inside another component's useEffect dependency array must return a referentially stable object across renders in tests that actually mount (react-dom/client + act), or the effect re-fires every render and can spin a vitest worker at ~100% CPU indefinitely instead of failing with a normal assertion error — it looks like a hang, not a red test.
learnings.action: Any new test that mounts (not just renderToStaticMarkup's) a component consuming a mocked context inside a useEffect dep array should hoist the mock's return value to a stable module-level constant.

learnings.insight: AC-9 (matchmaking timer ticking), AC-19 (Find-me scrollIntoView), and AC-27 (375px viewport overflow + 44x44 targets) are interaction/viewport behaviors that a unit render (renderToStaticMarkup or a happy-dom mount without a real layout engine) cannot meaningfully assert — happy-dom does not compute layout, so overflow/scroll assertions there would be theater, not evidence.
learnings.action: qa-acceptance should verify these three with the existing Playwright e2e setup (app/tests/e2e/) or an explicit manual procedure, not accept a unit test as proof for AC-9/19/27.
